newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: MPC says strong demand for high-end flats.
newsitem.headline: MPC says strong demand for high-end flats.

text.p: Diversified concern Metro Pacific Corp said on Tuesday it had seen strong buying interest for its luxury condominiums under construction at the edge of Manila's Makati business district.

Metro Pacific said the Pacific Plaza Towers project, the flagship condominium building in the emerging Bonifacio city, has already broken even days after it was granted the licence to sell by the Housing Land Use and Regulatory Board.

"We have experienced a strong take-up and have already reached our break-even sales point for the project. From here on, we are considering a marketing strategy which will allow us to capture enhanced values as the construction progresses," Pacific Plaza Towers Inc senior vice-president Conchitina Bernardo said in a statement.
The 300-square metre condominiums will be sold for between 29 million pesos to 33 million pesos each. The twin towers will have 194 units each. Buyers are required to make a 25 percent downpayment.
The condominiums are located on a 1.5 hectare plot of land. Completion date is scheduled for December 1999.
The project is a joint venture with the state-owned Bases Conversion Development Authority. Metro Pacific, a diversified concern, is a unit of Hong Kong's First Pacific Co Ltd.
